note: The Ministry of Health registry lists each establishment twice, once in French and once in Arabic under two post ids, and the two posts are paired into one bilingual record; `refs.msp_twin` names the second post, so either id resolves to the record. The two posts usually sit at consecutive ids. This is what the twin-post recovery in packages/sante/scripts/fetch.mjs decided: the pairs it merged into one record, and every nearby candidate it refused, with the reason. A near post id is not evidence on its own, so a candidate must also pass a consonant-skeleton name check, a gap of two needs stronger name evidence than a gap of one, and an ambiguous candidate is left alone rather than guessed at. A handful of cities entered their two halves far enough apart that adjacency cannot reach them at all, and in each the two halves name nothing but the city; those pairs carry `decided_by: "pair_table"`, are asserted by hand in packages/sante/scripts/twin-pair-table.mjs and publish the second source each one rests on in `evidence`. The cases that table was asked about and left alone are listed in `unpaired_candidates`, with what is missing. Regenerated by `npm run fetch` in packages/sante.

unpaired_candidates.facility: Skikda, the establishment the registry calls public
unpaired_candidates.why: Skikda city publishes an 'Etablissement hospitalier' and an 'Etablissement Public Hospitalier', and both carry the city name and nothing else. Separating them needs a source that says which Skikda hospital is the public establishment and which is not, in both languages. OpenStreetMap has two hospital buildings in the city, way/253913494 'Nouvel Hopital Abderezzak Bouhara' with no Arabic name at all and way/253914659 'Hopital de Skikda' / 'مستشفى سكيكدة', which is a toponym carrying neither legal class. Checked 2026-10-22: no ministry page, Journal Officiel text, Wikidata item or OpenStreetMap element names either establishment by its class in both languages, so both halves stay separate records.

unpaired_candidates.facility: Ouargla, the establishment the registry calls public
unpaired_candidates.why: Ouargla reads like Skikda, one 'Etablissement hospitalier' and one 'Etablissement Public Hospitalier' of the city, but with a second doubt on top of the first: checked 2026-10-22, only ONE general hospital of Ouargla city could be found in any source, way/303499771 'Hopital Mohamed Boudiaf' (and it carries no Arabic name). The other two hospitals found are a different legal class, the ophthalmology hospital way/304632975 and the mother-and-child EHS way/377113766. So it is not established that these four posts are two establishments at all: they may be one, entered under an older and a newer legal name, which would be a repeat merge of four posts rather than two pairs. Pairing them would decide that question by assumption.
